themes.name: Bohm and Stott Finally Delivering
themes.sample: After a brutal April, both corner pieces have erupted in May — Bohm on a double-digit hitting streak and Stott leading MLB in May RBI — giving the lineup real depth behind the top two.

themes.name: Sanchez and Wheeler Anchoring an Elite Rotation
themes.sample: Christopher Sanchez's scoreless streak and Cy Young chatter, combined with Wheeler outdueling Skeens, have fans treating the top of the rotation as a genuine strength heading into summer.

themes.name: Tuesday's Loss Is a One-Night Shrug
themes.sample: A 4-1 defeat to Chase Burns drew mostly calm reactions — 'we were due for a stinker, Burns is nasty' — though defensive miscues from Harper at first and Crawford in center drew familiar frustrations.

themes.name: Aaron Nola Anxiety Deepening
themes.sample: Nola's stuff looking flat and hittable, ERA climbing, and four years remaining on his deal have created the one genuinely dark cloud over an otherwise optimistic team picture.

themes.name: Mattingly Effect and Deadline Excitement Building
themes.sample: Six straight series wins under the new manager, plus buzz around a potential Japanese power bat acquisition, have fans feeling the front office and dugout are finally pointed in the same direction.

vibe_summary: Fans are riding a genuine wave of optimism after a torrid hot streak, shrugging off Tuesday's loss to an elite pitcher while Bohm, Stott, Sanchez, and Wheeler keep the belief very much alive — with only Aaron Nola casting a real shadow.
reasoning: The dominant mood is one of earned confidence: a scorching run under Mattingly, breakout performances from previously maligned roster pieces, and elite starting pitching have shifted the conversation from survival to October ambition. Tuesday's loss to Chase Burns was absorbed without panic — the overwhelming consensus was that a stinker was overdue and Burns simply pitched a great game. The one genuine fault line is Nola, where the analysis has moved from concern to something closer to dread, with his declining stuff and long contract creating a real drag on pitching confidence scores. Aidan Miller's injury opacity adds a secondary health note, but the broader roster health picture is stable enough that optimism holds.
